requirements.title: Effective network policy of a sandbox
requirements.rationale: A sandbox must reach the hub, its credentials' endpoints and what was allowed for its workspace, and nothing may weaken the rules that tie a credential to its endpoints.

criteria.condition: a sandbox is stored on a repository workspace or on a task fork
criteria.action: supply, through the workspace rule provider registered with package 45 and in the transaction that stores the sandbox, the id and the rule body of every workspace sandbox rule held at that moment by the workspace, or by the parent when the workspace is a task fork, ordered by created_at and then id, oldest first, which package 45 records with the sandbox beside the allow_proposals value of its profile snapshot
criteria.contract: the sandbox object's workspace_rules is the list of those rule ids in that order, [] when the workspace holds none; the same list is the workspace_rules metadata of parley.sandbox.create; the value of [sandbox].allow_workspace_rules and the sandbox's profile make no difference

setup: a real SQLite store in t.TempDir()
the fake runtime client of package 44
check.pseudocode: in internal/sandbox/policy_test.go, a table over {workspace 'demo' holding rules r1 (older) and r2; fork 'demo--a' of it; workspace 'empty' with no rule; 'demo' with allow_workspace_rules false; 'demo' with a second profile}: create a sandbox through the creation entry point of package 45; assert sandbox.workspace_rules == [r1.id, r2.id] for every row but 'empty', where it is []; assert the copies package 45 stored with the record equal r1.rule and r2.rule; assert the create event's metadata.workspace_rules equals the same list

criteria.condition: the provisioning work of package 45, after a create or after a start, asks the registered policy composer for the policy value of a sandbox
criteria.action: return one policy value made of the base policy of the sandbox's profile snapshot, the protected rules (the hub rule when the sandbox has a hub credential, then the rule of each attached credential in the order of the sandbox's credentials list), and the added rules (the recorded copies of the workspace rules in their recorded order, then the rules approved for this sandbox with either scope in the order they were decided)
criteria.contract: the CreateSandbox call of a create and the StartSandbox call of a start carry base == the profile's policy, protected == [hub rule, credential rules…] exactly as package 45 supplies them, and added == [workspace rule copies…, approved rules…]; a rule approved with scope workspace that is also among the recorded copies appears once

the fake runtime client of package 44
check.pseudocode: in internal/sandbox/policy_test.go, a table over {no workspace rule and no approval -> added == []; rules r1, r2 -> added == [r1.rule, r2.rule]; r1 plus one approval a1 with scope sandbox, composed for a start -> added == [r1.rule, a1.rule]; hub_access none -> protected holds the credential rules only; an approval with scope workspace on a sandbox created after the rule existed -> the rule once}: call ComposePolicy(sandbox) and the provisioning step with the fake runtime; assert the recorded policy's base, protected and added parts; assert protected is deep-equal to the rules the test passed in for the hub and for each credential

criteria.action: for any combination of base policy, workspace sandbox rules and approved rules, place the hub rule and every credential rule unchanged in the protected part of the policy and in no other part

for any sandbox, keep the recorded set of workspace sandbox rules fixed for the sandbox's life: a rule saved after the sandbox was created is not added to it, and a rule deleted after it was created stays in its workspace_rules and in the policy composed at every later start
criteria.contract: after a rule is deleted and another saved, an earlier sandbox's workspace_rules is unchanged and the policy composed for its next start carries the deleted rule's copy and not the new rule

criteria.condition: the base policy of the sandbox's profile contains a rule that refers to the provider of the hub credential
criteria.action: return an error from the policy composer, so that package 45 fails the provisioning before the sandbox is created at the runtime
criteria.contract: the sandbox reads with state failed, state_reason provision_failed and an error text that contains the profile's name and the words 'hub credential'; the runtime client received no create call for it

criteria.condition: the runtime rejects the composed policy when the sandbox is created at the runtime
criteria.action: end the sandbox as failed and, when the policy without workspace rules is accepted, find the rule to name, in the composer's Explain, by calling ValidatePolicy with the recorded workspace rules added one at a time in their order
criteria.contract: state failed with state_reason provision_failed; the error text contains the id of the first workspace sandbox rule with which the runtime rejects, or the profile's name when the runtime rejects the policy without any workspace rule; the text is at most 1,024 bytes

criteria.contract: the new sandbox's workspace_rules lists the rules the workspace holds now, including one promoted from the source sandbox; the policy the runtime receives for it holds no rule that was approved for the source with scope sandbox

requirements.title: Denials reported once per destination
requirements.rationale: A person watching a workspace needs to learn that an agent was blocked, without one retrying program flooding the event log.

criteria.condition: the runtime reports a denial for a sandbox whose (program, host, port) has not been reported for that sandbox
criteria.action: store the triple for the sandbox and write one parley.sandbox.deny event in the same transaction, with exposed secret values in its text replaced by package 45's redaction
criteria.contract: one event of type parley.sandbox.deny with actor system, resource_type sandbox, resource_id the sandbox id, workspace the sandbox's workspace, session_id the sandbox's, and metadata {program, host, port, method, path}, where method and path are null for a blocked connection and an exposed value of 8 or more characters inside path reads [redacted]

setup: a real SQLite store in t.TempDir()
the fake runtime client of package 44
the event component of package 52 on the same store
check.pseudocode: in internal/sandbox/collector_test.go, a table over denials the fake emits for a ready sandbox with session ses1 {('curl', 'example.org', 443, 'GET', '/a') -> metadata equal to the five values; ('git', '10.0.0.5', 22, no method, no path) -> method and path null; path containing the exposed value 'supersecretvalue' -> path contains '[redacted]' and not the value}: run one collector pass; assert exactly one new parley.sandbox.deny per row with actor 'system', resource_type 'sandbox', resource_id, workspace and session_id of the sandbox

criteria.condition: the runtime reports a denial whose (program, host, port) was already reported for that sandbox
criteria.action: write no event
criteria.contract: the event log gains no parley.sandbox.deny for a repeated triple, whatever its method and path; the same triple on another sandbox, and a triple that differs in program, host or port, is a first denial

criteria.action: for any denial the runtime reports for a sandbox the hub holds, first or repeated, add 1 to parley_sandbox_denials_total through the metrics recorder of package 44

criteria.condition: a sandbox is in state ready
criteria.action: follow that sandbox's policy log with Logs of the runtime client and take its deny entries, and stop following it within one collector pass after it leaves ready
criteria.contract: the collector holds one open policy log stream per ready sandbox and none for a sandbox in another state

criteria.condition: the runtime cannot be reached, or a policy log stream ends with an error
criteria.action: keep the hub running, open the stream again after the retry delay of 5 seconds, and treat every triple stored before as reported, including after a hub restart
criteria.contract: the collector returns no error to its caller and does not end; after the runtime answers again a new triple produces one event and a triple reported before the failure, or before a restart of the collector on the same store, produces none

requirements.title: Collecting proposals from the runtime
requirements.rationale: A blocked agent's request has to reach a person as a stored, listed item with the runtime's risk findings, and only from sandboxes whose operator allowed asking.

criteria.condition: a collector pass finds at the runtime a pending proposal that the hub has not stored, made by a sandbox whose recorded allow_proposals is true
criteria.action: store it as a proposal in state open with a new id of the form sbp_ followed by 32 lowercase hex characters, the rule, summary and findings as the runtime gave them and the runtime's proposal id, and write one parley.sandbox.proposal event in the same transaction
criteria.contract: a proposal {id, sandbox_id, rule, summary, findings, state: open, scope: null, workspace_rule_id: null, decided_by: null, decided_at: null, comment: null, created_at}; one event parley.sandbox.proposal with actor system, the sandbox as resource, its workspace and session_id, and metadata {proposal_id, summary, max_severity}, where max_severity is the highest finding severity in the order low < medium < high and null without findings

the fake runtime client of package 44
the event component of package 52 on the same store

criteria.condition: a collector pass finds a pending proposal whose runtime proposal id the hub already stored for that sandbox
criteria.action: store nothing and write no event
criteria.contract: after any number of passes over the same pending proposal there is one proposal record and one parley.sandbox.proposal event for it

criteria.condition: a collector pass finds a pending proposal made by a sandbox whose recorded allow_proposals is false
criteria.action: reject the proposal at the runtime, store nothing and write no event

requirements.title: Listing proposals and the checks every route shares
requirements.rationale: The person who decides needs the open requests of a sandbox with their findings, and a hub without sandboxes must answer every route the same way.

criteria.condition: a caller with sandboxes:read and read access to the workspace sends GET /api/v1/workspaces/:slug/sandboxes/:id/proposals
criteria.action: answer with the proposals of that sandbox in the state the query parameter state names, open when it is absent, ordered by created_at and then id, oldest first, paged by limit and cursor
criteria.contract: HTTP 200 with {items: [proposal…], next_cursor}; each item carries id, sandbox_id, rule, summary, findings, state, scope, workspace_rule_id, decided_by, decided_at, comment and created_at; a token bound to the workspace gets the same answer

requirements.title: Approving a proposal for its sandbox
requirements.rationale: A person, never the agent that asked, lets a sandbox reach one more destination, with the runtime's findings acknowledged when they are severe.

criteria.condition: a caller who is not a workspace-bound token, with sandboxes:write and write access to the sandbox's workspace, sends POST /api/v1/workspaces/:slug/sandboxes/:id/proposals/:proposal_id/approve for an open proposal with scope absent or sandbox, and the sandbox is provisioning or ready
criteria.action: add the proposal's rule to that sandbox's policy at the runtime and then, in one transaction, set the proposal to approved with scope sandbox, decided_by the caller, decided_at now and the given comment, store the rule as a rule approved for the sandbox, increase the sandbox's policy_revision by one and write one parley.sandbox.proposal_decided event
criteria.contract: HTTP 200 with the proposal {state: approved, scope: sandbox, workspace_rule_id: null, decided_by: {actor_type, actor_id, username}, decided_at, comment}; the sandbox's policy_revision is one higher; one event parley.sandbox.proposal_decided with the caller as actor, the sandbox as resource and metadata {proposal_id, decision: approved, acknowledged_findings, scope: sandbox, rule_id: null}; no workspace sandbox rule is saved

requirements.title: Rejecting a proposal
requirements.rationale: A refusal is a recorded decision too: the agent and the audit log learn who said no and why.

criteria.condition: a caller who is not a workspace-bound token, with sandboxes:write and write access to the sandbox's workspace, sends POST /api/v1/workspaces/:slug/sandboxes/:id/proposals/:proposal_id/reject for an open proposal
criteria.action: set the proposal to rejected with decided_by the caller, decided_at now and the given comment, write one parley.sandbox.proposal_decided event in the same transaction, and then tell the runtime that the proposal is rejected
criteria.contract: HTTP 200 with the proposal {state: rejected, scope: null, workspace_rule_id: null, decided_by, decided_at, comment}; one event with the caller as actor and metadata {proposal_id, decision: rejected, acknowledged_findings: false, scope: null, rule_id: null}; policy_revision is unchanged; the runtime client receives one RejectProposal call and no AddPolicyRule call; a proposal with a high finding needs no acknowledgement to be rejected

requirements.title: Promoting an approved rule to the workspace
requirements.rationale: The next sandbox on the workspace or on its forks should not have to ask again for a destination a person already allowed.

criteria.condition: a permitted caller approves an open proposal with scope workspace and the workspace that will hold the rule has no identical rule and fewer than 50 rules
criteria.action: do what an approval for the sandbox does and, in the same transaction, save the rule as a workspace sandbox rule with a new id of the form sbr_ followed by 32 lowercase hex characters, the proposal's rule, summary and findings, from_proposal, created_by the caller and created_at now, record scope workspace and the rule's id on the proposal, and write parley.sandbox.proposal_decided and parley.sandbox.rule_add
criteria.contract: HTTP 200 with the proposal {state: approved, scope: workspace, workspace_rule_id: <rule id>}; policy_revision is one higher; GET …/sandbox-rules lists the rule with from_proposal {sandbox_id, proposal_id, workspace}; the proposal_decided event's metadata has scope workspace and rule_id the rule's id; one event parley.sandbox.rule_add with the caller as actor, resource_type sandbox_rule, resource_id the rule id, workspace the holding workspace, session_id the sandbox's and metadata {rule_id, summary, max_severity, from_proposal}

execution_paths.title: A blocked agent asks for a destination and a developer approves it for the workspace

steps.action: runs a program in its sandbox on the fork demo--a that connects to registry.example.org:443, which no rule allows
blocks the connection and reports the denial; the workload then proposes a rule for that destination with the runtime's own mechanism
the collector reads the denial and emits parley.sandbox.deny, then finds the pending proposal, stores it as open and emits parley.sandbox.proposal
runs parley sandbox proposals demo--a <sandbox id>, reads the finding, and runs parley sandbox approve demo--a <sandbox id> <proposal id> --scope workspace --acknowledge-findings
sends GET …/proposals and then POST …/proposals/<proposal id>/approve with scope workspace, and prints the answers

checks that the caller is no bound token and can write to the parent demo, adds the rule to the sandbox at the runtime, saves it as a workspace sandbox rule of demo, raises policy_revision, emits parley.sandbox.proposal_decided and parley.sandbox.rule_add, and answers 200
creates a second sandbox on another fork of demo
records the rule's id in the new sandbox's workspace_rules and creates it at the runtime with a policy that carries the rule after the hub rule and the credential rules

setup: a hub started in-process on 127.0.0.1:0 with an empty data directory and a [sandbox] section with one profile that allows proposals; the OpenShell gateway is the fake runtime client of package 44, the only stand-in
a workspace demo, two task forks of it, a user who owns demo with an API key, and a ready sandbox on the first fork
the fake runtime is told to emit one denial of ('npm', 'registry.example.org', 443) and one pending proposal with a high finding for that sandbox
end_state: the proposal reads approved with scope workspace and a workspace_rule_id, and the first sandbox's policy_revision is 1
parley sandbox rules demo prints one rule whose from_proposal.workspace is the first fork's slug
the event log holds, in this order, one parley.sandbox.deny, one parley.sandbox.proposal, one parley.sandbox.proposal_decided and one parley.sandbox.rule_add whose workspace is demo
the second sandbox's workspace_rules holds the rule's id and the fake runtime's create call for it carries the rule among the added rules

execution_paths.title: A developer deletes a workspace sandbox rule and earlier sandboxes keep it

steps.action: runs parley sandbox rules demo and then parley sandbox rule-delete demo <rule id>
sends GET /api/v1/workspaces/demo/sandbox-rules and DELETE /api/v1/workspaces/demo/sandbox-rules/<rule id>, and prints {"id": "<rule id>", "status": "deleted"}
removes the rule, emits parley.sandbox.rule_remove on demo and answers 204, changing no sandbox
creates a new sandbox on demo
creates the new sandbox with an empty workspace_rules and a policy without the rule, while the earlier sandbox still lists the rule
